warnings.why: The Cayman Islands has a service- and finance-dominated economy with virtually no manufacturing sector, making an 85.5% high-tech manufactured export share extremely unrealistic and likely driven by re-exports or trade data classification errors.

Samoa has a very small manufacturing base focused mainly on light agricultural processing, so a 76.7% share of high-tech exports is implausible and likely reflects a data collection error or misclassification of non-manufactured goods.
Iceland's goods exports are dominated by aluminum and fish products; while it has niche tech, a 54% high-tech manufactured export share is far too high for its actual industrial output.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
